p: Hi, I'm Tom. I'm an EE grad student at Ashford Poly and I spend way too much time pointing FFTs at things that aren't supposed to have anything in them. In 1989 I found a 14.2 Hz carrier on a Nova Hart record. It turned into... this.

stardust.c is a coherent DBPSK demodulator for the 14.2 Hz sub-carrier on Nova Hart's SYNTHESIS (Orion Records, 1984). Public domain. It runs on a Mac Plus, a PC-98, a Samsung SPC-1000, a 386, an ES-1841 and (I'm told) an Amiga 500.

p: Informal supplementary notes for EE 471. The official course materials are on the department server; this mirror exists because students asked for something they could read from home over a modem.

From 1989 to 1993 I used the SYNTHESIS carrier as a classroom example of confirmation bias in spectral analysis. I was wrong. I now use it as a classroom example of a professor's confirmation bias in spectral analysis.
Exercise: given a 64 Hz decimated record of 40 minutes, estimate carrier frequency to 0.001 Hz using (a) periodogram, (b) Welch, (c) a phase-locked loop. Discuss why (c) wins.

Dr. Reiss's 1989 claim that Nova Hart's pitch deviations sit 7.1 sigma outside the human distribution has now been replicated by three groups, including mine. I do not know what it means. Students: a result you cannot explain is not a result you get to ignore. That is the actual lesson.
'The key is the pitch of my voice.' The last sustained vocal note of 'Threshold' is F#4 (369.99 Hz). 369.99 / 14.2 = 26.056. Not an integer. Close to 26 though.

p: For eleven years I transferred other people's reels to new media at the Fennimore Sound Archive. You learn to hear a machine's personality: how its capstan breathes, how its heads age. You also learn when something on a tape was put there by a person.

Delivered 30 November 1982. Grey box, Orion Records 'Special Projects' label, no paperwork. 15 ips, quarter-inch, full-track mono. On playback: silence, to the ear. On the meters: a slow, perfectly regular breathing. I did the transfer, logged it, and -- against every rule I ever enforced -- ran a cassette off the monitor feed because I wanted to understand it.
The reel was recalled on 2 July 1986. My cassette was not. In December 1994, running Tom's decoder, it gave us line 13.

homepage.title: Nova Hart à Paris - une enquête

p: En mars 1985, Nova Hart devait « passer » neuf jours à Paris pour la promotion du pressage français de SYNTHESIS. Personne ne l'a vue. Elle est apparue uniquement en duplex satellite, sur Antenne 2, depuis un studio que personne n'a pu situer.

En revanche, un homme aux yeux noisette -- verts, puis bleus, selon la lumière -- a visité trois fois une petite boutique de radioamateur rue de Rome. Le propriétaire, aujourd'hui retraité, se souvient : « Il voulait un récepteur capable de descendre très bas. Je lui ai dit que personne n'émet à quatorze hertz. Il a souri : ce n'est pas pour moi, c'est pour Nova. Ce n'est pas une émission, c'est une fissure. »

Le pressage français porte la ligne 6 : DO NOT WORSHIP THE COPY. Nous l'avons décodée en 1990 sur un compatible PC et diffusée sur le service Minitel 3615 STARDUST. Depuis l'arrivée de Luna Gray chez Orion en avril 1990, cette ligne est devenue un slogan.
